strengths: Novel structural approach using uniform spanning trees for principled sequence randomization in AR models, balancing flexibility with spatial coherence
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figures 1-2) explaining the core contribution
Comprehensive experimental methodology including multiple baselines, ablation studies (Tables 2-3), and detailed hyperparameter configurations
Well-designed evaluation protocol with multiple metrics (FID, IS, Precision, Recall) and fair model capacity comparisons
Addresses a genuine limitation of conventional AR models' inability to flexibly change inference sequence orders
Reproducible work with mentioned code availability and complete experimental details
weaknesses: Marginal empirical improvements: STAR-XXL achieves 338.8 FID tied with RandAR-XXL baseline (Table 1), with most variants showing only minor gains that do not justify added complexity
Weak theoretical justification: lacks rigorous analysis for why spanning trees specifically are superior; claims about 'maintaining prior knowledge' remain intuitive rather than proven
Unconvincing downstream task evaluation: image inpainting results (Figure 6, Table 2) are mixed and inconsistent, with modest improvements that do not demonstrate clear practical utility
Missing computational overhead analysis: no quantification of costs from spanning tree sampling and BFS traversal, critical given marginal empirical gains
Narrow experimental scope: only ImageNet-1k at 256×256 tested; no evaluation on other datasets or higher resolutions; limited to FID/IS metrics without perceptual metrics or human evaluation
Disconnected conditional entropy analysis: Figures 3-4 analyze prediction entropy patterns but fail to establish clear connection to visual generation quality
Ad-hoc design choices: random masking strategy for inpainting (Appendix B) lacks principled justification and appears orthogonal to the spanning tree contribution
Limited downstream task diversity: only image inpainting tested; broader evaluation on super-resolution, editing, or other applications needed to support flexibility claims
No failure case analysis or discussion of when spanning trees underperform, limiting insights into method applicability

strengths: Novel conceptual approach using spanning trees to structure autoregressive visual generation is creative and theoretically motivated
Comprehensive ablation studies (Tables 2-3) provide systematic investigation of different components and design choices
Solid theoretical grounding showing how uniform spanning trees preserve prior knowledge (center bias, locality) compared to random permutation, with clear entropy analysis
Enables flexible sequence order inference while maintaining training efficiency - a genuine practical capability
Clear and effective visualizations (Figures 1-2) that communicate the core concepts well
Provides mathematical justification connecting lattice theory to image generation
weaknesses: Critical performance deficit on the main task: STAR-XXL (FID=338.8) significantly underperforms simpler baselines like UViT-XL/2 (FID=278.2) despite having more parameters, making the method impractical for deployment

Fundamental contradiction in core claims: Table 2 shows random+spanning-tree ordering (FID=282.5) performs substantially worse than random+random (FID=234.9) for generation, directly contradicting the theoretical motivation that spanning trees should improve performance

Weak justification for why theoretical benefits don't materialize empirically - the paper acknowledges 'degraded sampling performance' but provides no satisfactory explanation or investigation into the cause

Image inpainting evaluation is insufficient: Figure 6 shows STAR has higher FID than RAR across most masking ratios, contradicting the claimed strength; only basic masking ratio evaluation without other inpainting benchmarks
No statistical significance testing or error bars despite small metric differences, making it unclear whether differences are meaningful
Limited comparative analysis: missing comparisons with recent strong baselines and no computational cost analysis despite likely additional overhead from spanning tree sampling
Mismatch between theoretical motivation (spanning trees preserve structure) and empirical reality (random permutation outperforms), suggesting core premise may be flawed
Technical novelty is limited: spanning tree sampling and BFS traversal are established techniques; the algorithmic contribution is modest
Practical value unclear: for image editing (the main claimed benefit), STAR underperforms RAR making adoption unjustifiable from practitioners' perspective
Insufficient analysis of failure modes: paper lacks investigation into where and why STAR falls short compared to baselines

strengths: Novel spanning tree-based sequence ordering strategy with clear theoretical motivation for balancing flexibility and performance in AR visual generation
Comprehensive experimental validation including extensive comparisons with multiple baseline categories, thorough ablation studies (Tables 2-3), and analysis across model scales
Strong theoretical grounding with insightful analysis of conditional prediction entropy (Figures 3-4) demonstrating importance of token locality and prior knowledge preservation
Practical applicability with minimal architectural changes required, enabling broad integration into existing AR models
Well-structured presentation with effective visualizations and clear mathematical formulation; code availability enhances reproducibility
Demonstrates both competitive generation performance and improved inpainting capabilities with flexible sequence ordering
weaknesses: Marginal performance improvements over baselines—STAR-XXL FID (1.55) is actually slightly worse than RandAR-XXL (1.48), with identical IS scores (338.8), questioning practical significance of the approach
Limited experimental scope: evaluation only on ImageNet-1k; testing on additional datasets (COCO, CelebA) and higher resolutions (512×512, 1024×1024) would strengthen claims
Insufficient computational analysis: no discussion of overhead for spanning tree sampling and BFS traversal during training; training time and inference latency not compared with baselines

Theoretical justification could be stronger: lacks formal analysis of optimality or convergence properties; no exploration of alternative graph sampling strategies or theoretical comparison with other traversal methods
Inpainting evaluation primarily qualitative with limited quantitative assessment; evaluation restricted to variable masking ratios rather than standard inpainting benchmarks
Core contribution is sequence ordering rather than architectural innovation; underlying ViT-based AR Transformer is standard, somewhat limiting the scope of contribution

Section 3.3 on postfix completion traversal is dense and underexplained; Algorithm 1's practical implementation details underspecified; gap between theoretical spanning trees and actual implementation unclear
Missing analysis of failure modes, sensitivity to spanning tree selection strategies, and incomplete exploration of alternative traversal orderings (DFS vs. BFS)

strengths: Well-motivated sequence order strategy using spanning trees that elegantly balances spatial structure and flexibility, with clear articulation of why this middle ground is superior to both fixed orders and random permutations

Comprehensive experimental evaluation including extensive ablation studies (locality effects, center bias, conditional entropy analysis, DFS/BFS comparison) that provide good insights into design choices
Practical architectural simplicity requiring only minimal modifications to standard decoder-only Transformers, making the method easily adoptable by practitioners
Competitive empirical results on ImageNet-1k image generation with STAR-XXL achieving FID scores comparable to or better than several baseline methods
Thorough presentation with clear motivation, well-organized methodology, effective visualizations, and detailed implementation details in supplementary material
Solid theoretical grounding in entropy analysis and intuitive explanations for why spanning tree properties preserve prior knowledge while enabling flexibility
weaknesses: Significantly limited experimental scope: evaluation only on ImageNet-1k at single resolution (256×256) with no experiments on other benchmarks (COCO, CelebA-HQ, LSUN) or higher resolutions (512×512+) standard in recent visual generation work

Incremental contribution: the core innovation is a token sequencing strategy rather than a new architecture, loss function, or fundamental modeling approach—essentially a better way to order existing tokens

Incomplete theoretical justification: entropy convergence conjecture (Section 3.2) stated but not rigorously proven; connection between spanning tree properties and claimed performance improvements lacks formal analysis

Unfair baseline comparisons in Table 1 with varying model sizes (261M–804M parameters) and unclear if all methods trained identically, making it difficult to isolate the sequence order strategy's contribution
Mixed empirical results in key settings: Figure 7 shows RAR outperforming STAR on inpainting at lower masking ratios (0.1–0.3); Table 2 shows performance gaps unexplained by authors

Computational overhead not thoroughly analyzed: Table 4 mentions 0.56 ms per instance for spanning tree sampling without context; missing total inference time comparisons and training cost analysis of handling multiple sequence orders

Postfix completion mechanism has acknowledged limitation: Appendix A admits violations of core masking assumptions are common in practice, contradicting claimed theoretical validity and requiring ad-hoc multi-turn inference solutions
Missing analysis of failure modes, design trade-offs, and clear guidance for practitioners on when to use STAR versus alternatives
Representation learning analysis (Section 5, Figure 9) feels tangential to main contribution and appears disconnected from core narrative
No explicit discussion of method limitations or broader societal impact, which are expected in modern venue submissions

strengths: Novel sequence ordering strategy using uniform spanning trees that creatively addresses the tension between fixed and random sequence orders in autoregressive visual generation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple baselines and detailed comparisons across both generation and inpainting tasks
Thorough ablation studies (Section 4.3) systematically analyzing design choices including locality, center bias, and conditional model entropy
Technically sound implementation with formal algorithms and clear mathematical notation
Visually plausible qualitative results across diverse object categories with good visual quality
weaknesses: Marginal empirical improvements: STAR-XXL achieves only 0.08 FID improvement over RandAR-XXL (3.52 vs 3.60), raising questions about practical significance relative to added complexity

Weak theoretical justification for why uniform spanning trees specifically are necessary; no comparison with alternative tree traversal strategies; paper acknowledges that permutation AR modeling fundamentally converges more slowly

Severely restrictive assumptions for image inpainting: requires masks not covering all corners and dividing observations into disconnected graphs, limiting practical applicability; supplementary material defers addressing violations
Computational overhead from spanning tree sampling and rejection sampling not thoroughly analyzed; claims of 'negligible' cost lack rigorous wall-clock time comparisons
Limited evaluation scope: only ImageNet-1k at 256×256; no evaluation on other datasets, higher resolutions, or recent diffusion-based inpainting methods for comparison
Unclear practical motivation: paper does not convincingly demonstrate when flexible sequence ordering matters in practice or why practitioners would need multiple orders at inference
Comparison fairness concerns: many baseline results are from published papers rather than direct re-implementations with potentially different training procedures and compute budgets
Modest improvements may not justify adoption; Table 2 shows inconsistent inpainting results where RandAR sometimes outperforms STAR
Limited analysis of failure modes with all presented results appearing as successes; missing negative results or challenging scenarios
Overclaimed contribution: the image editing 'building block' is essentially the same approach applied to masking rather than a distinct conceptual contribution

strengths: Novel and creative use of uniform spanning trees to balance random permutation and fixed sequence order approaches in autoregressive visual generation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with extensive comparisons to multiple strong baselines on both generation and inpainting tasks
Thorough ablation studies analyzing key components (locality, center bias, search strategies) with clear insights from conditional entropy analysis
Strong empirical results showing competitive or superior performance on both image generation and inpainting, with particularly notable improvements on inpainting
Practical benefits: enables region-level image modification with minimal architectural changes to standard Decoder-only Transformer
Efficient implementation with negligible computational overhead (0.56 ms per instance)
Clear and well-structured presentation with effective visualizations of the core concepts
Solid theoretical intuition connecting prior knowledge preservation to spanning tree properties
weaknesses: Evaluation limited to ImageNet-1k at 256×256 resolution; no experiments at higher resolutions or diverse datasets (COCO, CelebA, etc.)
Theoretical justification lacks rigor—claims about sufficiency and optimality of spanning trees are primarily empirical rather than formally proven
Incomplete computational efficiency analysis; detailed training time comparisons and sampling efficiency quantification relative to baselines is missing
Rejection sampling efficiency for postfix completion not thoroughly analyzed; failure rates under different masking conditions not clearly reported
Assumption that masks do not cover all corners or create disconnected regions is stated as 'relatively rare' but lacks empirical validation
Generalization to video, 3D data, or other modalities unclear; approach inherently designed for 2D image structure
Some experimental details relegated to supplementary materials; dense exposition in places makes the method harder to follow
Limited analysis of failure modes, convergence behavior, or hyperparameter sensitivity
